correctness.rationale: Acyclic input gives exactly strict reachability: when a pair is not reachable, adjoining its reverse does not create a cycle and a topological order witnesses nonentailment. Cyclic input has no models and closes to all oriented pairs. Each two-edge directed path missing its shortcut, and each opposite-arrow pair, forces an exact premise in any iterative basis: no proper subset allows the first nontrivial inference. These rules suffice. For simultaneous directness a path's endpoints force its entire simple-path premise, and a proper cycle forces its entire premise by choosing a conclusion incident to an outside vertex. A spanning directed cycle needs only its proper path premises, which already supply every missing oriented pair. Counting the distinct path and cycle premises gives the two displayed sums; the cycle sum divided by n! tends to zero by splitting at n/2. Midpoint subdivision adds comparisons along paths of length at most 2^t in t rounds. A proper cycle yields an opposite-arrow pair by L−1 using forward cyclic distances at most ceil((n−1)/2), whereas a spanning cycle yields all pairs by L without explosion. A spanning path forces L rounds in the stated iterative basis. An independent finite closure-from-models calculation counted minimal nonclosed sets and premises compelled in one round for n=3 and 4, giving (9,9) and (30,62). The combinatorial proof, not this enumeration, covers all n.
residual_risks: Counts are grouped by premise, with no auxiliary attributes and strictly simultaneous firing. The depth is for the displayed iterative basis, not a lower bound for unrestricted-size bases.

value.rationale: Linear precedence constraints are a natural closure model with consistency and transitivity. On exactly the same attributes the result quantifies the cost of insisting on one simultaneous pass: factorial many grouped premises instead of cubic many with logarithmic depth. The reason proper cycles but not spanning cycles require new direct premises identifies which inconsistent inputs cause additional rules; this is not just standard transitive-closure doubling.
residual_risks: This is a grouped-rule count and synchronous depth gap, not a claim about running time, unit rules, or an ordered pass.
